items.q: What actually happened in Cardiff on 14 September 2026?
items.a: SNP, Plaid Cymru, and Sinn Féin signed a **party MoU**. First time all three Celtic administrations are led by exit-or-unity parties. Not a referendum, not an Act, not a breakup.

items.q: What is the video's one-line verdict?
items.a: The UK **can look like** it is dissolving and **will not** dissolve on this memo. Slogan is independence. Goods are tax, energy, spend, and EU-adjacent exceptions.
A close poll (~50/50) plus **energy and fiscal control**, with London as the backstop if the experiment fails. Second vote still needs Westminster.

items.q: Why is Welsh independence a weaker file?
items.a: Thin yes-camp. Lives on **transfers** after deindustrialization. The HS2 jab: pay for a line that never comes. More money and powers, not a flag.

items.q: Why is Northern Ireland not a Scotland clone?
items.a: **Good Friday** already encodes a dual-consent path to Irish unity. Sinn Féin is in office. Unionists still block a border poll. The Protocol left NI closer to the EU than Great Britain.

**Westminster.** 2022 Supreme Court: Holyrood cannot legislate a vote alone. GFA: a border poll only if the Secretary of State judges majority support. Burnham: off limits before the next general election.

items.q: What would actually raise breakup odds?
items.a: If London **cannot fund the periphery**. Under-45s are already more exit-curious. The cheque is the glue; glue failure is the clock, not this week's memo.
